text.p: Following are the main stories in Tuesday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Several Cabinet ministers, opposition party members, corporate leaders, trade unionists, academicians and others will, for the first time, meet on Saturday to address the problem of corruption.
-- More than 1,000 people, including foreign workers, were made homeless when a fire destroyed 179 squatter houses in Kampung Cenderamata II near eastern Sabah's Kota Kinabalu town on Monday.
-- It will soon be an offence to make a false report against someone for corrupt practices under a proposed amendment to the Prevention of Corruption Act, Acting Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said.

-- Petroliam Nasional Bhd (Petronas) saw greater diversification and expansion of its operations to post a record group pre-tax profit of 12.39 billion ringgit for the year ended March 31, 1997, a 44.7 percent increase from 1996.
-- KLCC Holdings Sdn Bhd, developer of the Kuala Lumpur City Centre (KLCC) project, plans to be listed on the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange main board by year-end.
-- The ringgit stood its ground yesterday, closing marginally down at 2.5355/75 against the U.S. dollar in an overall tough trading day, from 2.5045/55 last Friday.
-- Malaysia welcomes the proposal by Cambodia's Second Prime Minister Hun Sen to hold a free and fair election to pave the way for the formation of a government of the people's choice.
